under it. So the verb renames what the copy binds before putting it back, and
the new name is the one nothing else in the function is using.

which is the next thing missing.

note: The registers that decide what runs hold the functions themselves, not their

It is worth saying what that mistake looks like, because it does not look
like one. A written word dropped into a list of functions is rewritten by
the auto pass into

as though it were a live entry — and running nothing at all, in the one kind
of list whose whole job is to run what it holds. Adding the gate below by

marks where that passage begins — a bookmark that says what it means, which
no line number does. Pairing it with a verb it was never written for is the
point: neither half knows the other.
